subject: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Trying to lock the runtime release train cutoff today.

Can each owner reply w/ (a) which PRs we want in the train, (b) required checks, and (c) your “if perf-canary fails” fallback (flag off / revert / hold)?

Candidate PRs from the sprint that are queued/landing:
- PR 10621: kernel-selection + quant-mode tracing spans (flagged)
- PR 10622: FP8 attention tuning (H100/H200)
- PR 10623: INT8 GEMM conversion overhead reductions + fusions
- PR 10624: scheduler batch-size cap override for quantized decode (tail latency)
- PR 10625: fix auto-selector picking FP16 kernel for specific INT8 shapes (guard + unit test)
- PR 10626: perf-lab build target (repro container metadata)
- PR 10627: numeric drift checks FP8/INT8 vs FP16 baseline (CI gating)
- PR 10628: KV-cache conversion avoidance in decode
- PR 10629: runtime knob to force quant kernel family (A/B)
- PR 10630: FP8 prefill alignment fix for long-context prompts
- PR 10633: deprecate legacy INT8 toggle; consolidate flags
- PR 10635: L40S fused op revert / GPU-conditional disable

Also note: SUP-6193 is still open on customer-reported INT8 latency regression; we need to be careful about anything that can move p95.

[Attachment: runtime-release-train-checklist_v2025-10-10.docx]

— Connor
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 9:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

On required checks:

Hard gates I’d like before we ship anything that changes math or kernel selection:
1) PR 10627 drift checks green in CI on at least A100 + H100 (the small prompt set). If it’s too flaky, we need an allowlist + explicit exceptions recorded.
2) perf-canary quant job (perf-canary/pr_188 + comparator changes in /pr_189) green on the pinned matrix (A100, H100, L40S; H200 if Sean has capacity).
3) benchmark-lab results artifact + tags include runtime commit + GPU clocks (10621 helps, but also needs the structured perf log events in 10631 if we can’t land that yet).

If perf-canary fails after merge:
- Prefer “ship but default-off” only if we have a safe runtime knob AND we can validate the default path remains identical.
- Otherwise: revert in the release branch. For kernel-level changes, I don’t trust config-only mitigation unless we have clean separation.

Sahana


From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Kim <grace.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Yuki Sato <yuki.sato@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Kernel team view (risk-based):

Recommend we land in this train:
- 10625 (auto-selector fix): low risk, correctness fix + unit test. This also blocks one of our INT8 perf attribution issues.
- 10630 (FP8 prefill alignment fix): correctness + perf on long-context prompts; we have a targeted regression test.
- 10621 (tracing spans): flagged; needed for ongoing attribution.
- 10629 (force kernel family knob): useful for follow-up A/B; should be safe if default behavior unchanged.

Recommend we HOLD unless canary + drift checks are squeaky clean:
- 10622 (FP8 attention tuning): perf-positive on H100/H200 microbench; still want one more end-to-end pass (streaming chat p95).
- 10623 (INT8 GEMM conversion/fusion): biggest perf win but also most surface area; we saw one intermittent mismatch on L40S earlier in the week (may be addressed by 10635).
- 10628 (KV cache conversion avoidance): likely safe but touches decode loop; want perf-canary signal.

If perf-canary fails:
- For 10622/10623/10628: revert in release branch. For 10621/10629: can keep (feature flagged / knobs) unless evidence of overhead.

-Hiro


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@redwoodinference.com>, Julian Moore <julian.moore@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 10:22 AM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Scheduler:

PR 10624 (batch-size cap override for quantized decode) — I’m OK landing IF:
- It’s behind a config knob with a conservative default (off), OR default is no-op for non-quant paths.
- We run at least one mixed prompt-length scenario (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy) in benchmark-lab with streaming (TTFT/TPOT) and confirm we don’t regress throughput > ~2% while improving p95 TPOT.

PR 10632 (queue wait histograms by quant mode/phase) isn’t on your list, but if it’s already in flight I’m supportive since it helps interpret canary failures.

If perf-canary fails:
- If failure is only in tail latency (p95/p99) and we can attribute it to the override: disable knob by default + annotate release notes.
- If correctness/perf is broadly impacted: revert.

Sofia


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 11:05 AM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Perf-lab/canary status:

- Nightly quant-perf canary is running on A100 + H100 + L40S consistently now. H200 is still capacity constrained; I can do 1 run today but not guaranteed nightly until next week.
- Biggest current source of noise is node contention during EU morning. We mitigated some by pinning clocks + isolating jobs, but it’s not perfect.

My ask: please treat “single red” as a triage signal, not an auto-revert, unless comparator flags it as statistically significant (pr_189 improves this, but we’re still tuning).

For this release train, I’d like the following to be mandatory before we merge risky perf changes:
- Canary results show at least 3 consecutive passes on A100/H100 for the quant scenarios.
- If L40S shows any correctness instability, we should ship 10635 (GPU-conditional disable) or hold the fusion changes.

[Attachment: quant-perf-canary-last-7-runs.png]

Sean


From: Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 11:42 AM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Benchmark-lab view:

If we ship changes in this train, I strongly prefer landing 10626 (repro build target) alongside, otherwise we’ll keep arguing about “which container actually ran.”

Also: 10621 helps but we still want 10631 structured perf log events for ingestion. If 10631 is too late for this train, I can live with it as long as:
- kernel-selection spans emit chosen kernel + quant mode + shapes under flag
- benchmark runner captures GPU clocks + driver + runtime commit in the results JSON

I can run an updated full matrix this weekend ONLY if release branch stays stable by EOD today.

Rina


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 12:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Thanks all. Proposed cut for the release train (assuming CI + canary):

“Must land (low-risk / plumbing / correctness fixes)”
- 10625 auto-selector guard + unit test
- 10630 FP8 prefill alignment fix (long-context)
- 10621 tracing spans (flagged)
- 10626 perf-lab build target
- 10627 numeric drift checks in CI (gate)
- 10629 force-quant-kernel-family knob (default no-op)
- 10635 L40S conditional disable / revert fused op (if it’s required for stability)

“Conditional (needs 3x canary pass + drift check + at least 1 end-to-end benchmark run)”
- 10622 FP8 attention tuning (H100/H200)
- 10623 INT8 GEMM conversion/fusion
- 10628 KV cache conversion avoidance
- 10624 scheduler batch cap override (default-off unless Sofia says safe)

Contingency if perf-canary fails late:
- For conditional items: revert on release branch.
- For must-land: keep unless canary shows overhead attributable to tracing; then disable flag by default.

Mateo — can you confirm this aligns w/ what you want to ship given SUP-6193 risk?

— Connor


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 1:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Aligns.

Given SUP-6193 (INT8 latency regression report), I’m not comfortable shipping 10623 unless we have:
- Drift checks clean (10627)
- Canary clean for 3 consecutive runs on A100/H100, and no new L40S correctness flags
- Rina has at least one end-to-end streaming chat run that shows p95 TPOT does not regress.

I do want 10625 + 10630 in regardless; those are correctness fixes and reduce the chance of silent fallback/selector weirdness.

10624: keep default-off this train. We can flip in a targeted hosted cohort later with clear rollback.

If canary goes red after merge, I’d rather revert conditional PRs than accumulate “flags we promise not to enable.”

Mateo


From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 2:33 PM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

If 10621 lands, please ensure span fields include:
- quant_mode (fp8/int8/fp16)
- chosen_kernel_id / family
- shape summary (m/n/k or seq_len/batch where relevant)

We can wire this into the quant perf dashboard panels quickly, but only if tag naming is stable.

Also: if we do a revert due to canary, please drop a note in #eng-runtime with the runtime commit + reason. We’ve had “mystery regressions” before because the revert wasn’t visible to dashboard consumers.

[Attachment: draft-release-notes_quant-section.md]

Allison


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rina Kobayashi <rina.kobayashi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 4:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Quant changes for next runtime release train (FP8/INT8) — what lands + required gates

Decision recorded for this train:

IN (targeting merge by cutoff): 10621, 10625, 10626, 10627, 10629, 10630 (+ 10635 if L40S stability requires it)
CONDITIONAL/HOLD: 10622, 10623, 10628, 10624 (default-off; treat as post-release cohort experiment)

Gates (release branch):
- CI drift checks (10627) required
- perf-canary quant job: 3 consecutive passes A100/H100 (L40S must not show correctness issues)
- at least 1 benchmark-lab end-to-end streaming chat run for any conditional perf PR

Contingency:
- Canary red attributable to conditional PR => revert on release branch
- Canary red due to noise => Sean/Sahana triage; if inconclusive by T+4h, revert to unblock train

Talia — please mirror this into the release train tracker.

— Connor
